> **Pipeline step 04 — PSIS-LOO reliability audit.**
>
> **Purpose.** For every PSIS-LOO-scored TPS fit, reconstructs how many observations had Pareto
> k > 0.7 before moment matching and how many remained above it afterwards. Nothing is refit.
>
> **Inputs.** `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/`, `fits_tps_landscape/`. **Output.** a summary CSV (path in the
> notebook).

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Diagnostic companion to `01_tps_catch_models/tps_catch_landscape_models.Rmd` and
`01_tps_catch_models/tps_catch_wq_models.Rmd`. It answers one question for every saved fit: how many
observations had Pareto k > 0.7 in the raw PSIS-LOO — i.e. how many actually needed moment
matching — and how many were still above 0.7 afterwards.

WHY THIS HAS TO BE RECOMPUTED: `loo_moment_match()` overwrites `diagnostics$pareto_k` in place.
The saved fits (and the `loo_tps*.rds` sidecars) therefore carry only the POST-moment-match k,
with no record of the pre-MM values and no flag marking which observations were reprocessed. The
appended `*_output.txt` logs hold only `summary(fit)`, so the pre-MM diagnostics are not stored
anywhere. They are, however, fully recoverable: `log_lik()` is deterministic given the posterior
draws already inside each `.rds`, so re-running plain PSIS-LOO on those draws reproduces the
original pre-moment-match diagnostics exactly. NOTHING IS REFIT HERE — this notebook only reads.

The threshold is 0.7 because `brms:::loo_moment_match.brmsfit` defaults to `k_threshold = 0.7`,
so "k > 0.7" is exactly "was moment-matched".

The reconstruction self-validates: any fit with zero pre-MM exceedances must show an `elpd_shift`
of exactly 0, since moment matching had nothing to do. If a zero-exceedance fit shows a non-zero
shift, the reconstruction is wrong and the table should not be trusted.

Covers the two fit sets reported in the manuscript:
  * TPS landscape  — `fits_tps_landscape/fit_tps1..10.rds`   (n = 838 tows)
  * TPS water qual — `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/fit_tps_wq0..13.rds`  (n = 818 tows)

```{r}
library(brms)
library(loo)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Config. `OUT_CSV` is a diagnostics table, not a fit — it is written alongside the WQ fits but
never touches any `fit_*.rds`.
```{r}
LANDSCAPE_DIR <- "fits_tps_landscape"
WQ_DIR        <- "fits_tps_wq_Vfix"
OUT_CSV       <- file.path(WQ_DIR, "pareto_k_summary.csv")

K_THRESHOLD <- 0.7   # brms loo_moment_match default; "> K_THRESHOLD" == "was moment-matched"
```


###################################
Audit one fit.
Recomputes the pre-moment-match PSIS-LOO the same way brms does (log_lik -> relative_eff on the
exponentiated likelihood -> `loo()`), then reads the stored post-MM k off `fit$criteria$loo`.
Returns a one-row data frame; drops the ~29 MB fit before returning so peak memory stays flat.
########################################
```{r}
audit_one_fit <- function(path, label, k_threshold = K_THRESHOLD, verbose = TRUE) {
  fit <- readRDS(path)

  # --- pre-moment-match PSIS-LOO, as brms computes it before loo_moment_match() ---
  ll       <- log_lik(fit)                       # draws x obs
  nchains  <- fit$fit@sim$chains
  chain_id <- rep(seq_len(nchains), each = nrow(ll) / nchains)
  r_eff    <- loo::relative_eff(exp(ll), chain_id = chain_id)
  pre      <- loo::loo(ll, r_eff = r_eff)
  k_pre    <- pre$diagnostics$pareto_k

  # --- post-moment-match k + elpd, as stored on the fit ---
  has_mm <- !is.null(fit$criteria$loo)
  k_post <- if (has_mm) fit$criteria$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k else NA_real_

  out <- data.frame(
    fit             = label,
    n_obs           = length(k_pre),
    n_k_gt_thresh   = sum(k_pre > k_threshold),
    n_k_0.5_thresh  = sum(k_pre > 0.5 & k_pre <= k_threshold),
    pct_mm          = round(100 * sum(k_pre > k_threshold) / length(k_pre), 3),
    max_k_pre       = round(max(k_pre), 3),
    n_k_gt_thresh_post = if (has_mm) sum(k_post > k_threshold) else NA_integer_,
    pct_post        = if (has_mm) round(100 * sum(k_post > k_threshold) / length(k_pre), 3) else NA_real_,
    max_k_post      = if (has_mm) round(max(k_post), 3) else NA_real_,
    elpd_pre        = pre$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"],
    elpd_post       = if (has_mm) fit$criteria$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"] else NA_real_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  out$elpd_shift <- round(out$elpd_post - out$elpd_pre, 2)

  if (verbose) {
    cat(sprintf("%-16s n=%4d  pre k>%.1f: %3d (0.5-%.1f: %3d)  max_k_pre=%.3f  ->  post: %3d  max_k_post=%.3f\n",
                label, out$n_obs, k_threshold, out$n_k_gt_thresh, k_threshold,
                out$n_k_0.5_thresh, out$max_k_pre, out$n_k_gt_thresh_post, out$max_k_post))
  }
  rm(fit, ll, pre); gc()
  out
}

# Audit a whole set of fits given a directory, a filename prefix and the fit numbers.
audit_fit_set <- function(dir, prefix, nums, set_label, ...) {
  rows <- list()
  for (num in nums) {
    path <- file.path(dir, sprintf("%s%d.rds", prefix, num))
    if (!file.exists(path)) { warning("missing fit: ", path); next }
    r <- audit_one_fit(path, sprintf("%s%d", prefix, num), ...)
    r$set <- set_label
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- r
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

# Sanity check described in the header: zero pre-MM exceedances must mean zero elpd shift.
check_reconstruction <- function(tab, tol = 1e-6) {
  clean <- tab[tab$n_k_gt_thresh == 0, ]
  bad   <- clean[abs(clean$elpd_shift) > tol, ]
  if (nrow(bad)) {
    warning("reconstruction suspect for: ", paste(bad$fit, collapse = ", "))
  } else {
    message("OK: all ", nrow(clean), " fits with no pre-MM exceedances show zero elpd shift.")
  }
  invisible(bad)
}
```


###################################
Run the audit.
Reads every fit once (~29 MB each), so this takes a few minutes for the full 24.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
landscape <- audit_fit_set(LANDSCAPE_DIR, "fit_tps",    1:10, "landscape")
wq        <- audit_fit_set(WQ_DIR,        "fit_tps_wq", 0:13, "wq")

pareto_k_audit <- rbind(landscape, wq)
check_reconstruction(pareto_k_audit)

# Reported column order: counts and percentages first, elpd bookkeeping last.
pareto_k_summary <- pareto_k_audit[, c("set", "fit", "n_obs",
                                       "n_k_gt_thresh", "pct_mm", "max_k_pre",
                                       "n_k_gt_thresh_post", "pct_post", "max_k_post",
                                       "elpd_shift")]
print(pareto_k_summary, row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(pareto_k_summary, OUT_CSV, row.names = FALSE)
```


###################################
Set-level totals.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
for (s in unique(pareto_k_audit$set)) {
  x <- pareto_k_audit[pareto_k_audit$set == s, ]
  cat(sprintf("%-10s fits=%2d  obs=%5d  needed MM=%2d (%.3f%%)  still k>0.7 after MM=%2d (%.3f%%)  fits affected=%d\n",
              s, nrow(x), sum(x$n_obs), sum(x$n_k_gt_thresh),
              100 * sum(x$n_k_gt_thresh) / sum(x$n_obs),
              sum(x$n_k_gt_thresh_post),
              100 * sum(x$n_k_gt_thresh_post) / sum(x$n_obs),
              sum(x$n_k_gt_thresh > 0)))
}
```


###################################
Result as run on 2026-08-31 (written to `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/pareto_k_summary.csv`).

Landscape: 1 of 8,380 observations needed moment matching (0.012%), in `fit_tps1` alone
(max k 0.771); moment matching resolved it. All ten landscape fits end clean.

Water quality: 24 of 11,452 observations needed moment matching (0.210%), spread over 9 of the
14 fits, worst case 6 observations (0.733%) in `fit_tps_wq8` and `fit_tps_wq9`.

Moment matching did NOT fully resolve three WQ fits:
  * fit_tps_wq3 — 2 still above 0.7 (max k 0.942)
  * fit_tps_wq8 — 2 still above 0.7 (max k 0.854)
  * fit_tps_wq9 — 5 still above 0.7 (max k 1.022)
Their ELPD estimates are mildly unreliable. All three sit mid-pack in the LOOIC ranking (4th,
5th, 7th) and none is the selected model, so the model comparison is not driven by them. The one
worth reporting in the methods is `fit_tps_wq9`: k > 1 means infinite importance-sampling
variance, so the elpd contribution of those 5 points is effectively unestimated. The top-ranked
`fit_tps_wq11` and the base `fit_tps_wq0` are both clean (0 exceedances, max k 0.68 / 0.65).
########################################
